samples.summary: `--dry-run` paths return before the new `parseOutputFormat` guard, so a bogus `--format` is silently accepted (exit 0) instead of producing the documented `INVALID_FORMAT` error
samples.evidence: In `cells set` the dry-run block at cells.ts:52-60 runs and `return`s before the `try` that calls `parseOutputFormat(opts.format)` at line 63. Same ordering in `cells delete` (86-93 vs 96), `cells batch` (129-137 vs 140), `docs update`/`docs delete` (docs.ts:135-139 vs 141, 153-157 vs 160), `notes update`/`notes delete`, `slides update`/`slides delete`. By contrast `docs create`/`notes create`/`slides create` validate first (docs.ts:102 before the dry-run block at 103-106). Result: `wafflebase sheets cells set d A1 v --dry-run --format bogus` exits 0 with a dry-run body, while the same command without `--dry-run` exits 1 with `INVALID_FORMAT` — contradicting docs/design/cli.md §8.2 ("`--dry-run` validates inputs") and §8.1's "an unsupported `--format` value is rejected ... rather than ignored".

samples.summary: New `cell()` JSON-serialization is applied only to the single-object key/value path; the array path still renders nested values as `[object Object]`
samples.evidence: `cell()` (table.ts:7-10) is used only by `formatRecord` (line 24). The array branch still uses `String(row[key] ?? '')` for width computation (line 46) and for the rendered cells (line 53), so any array row containing a nested object/array still prints `[object Object]` under `--format table` — e.g. list endpoints whose items carry nested fields. The docstring's claim that it "Mirrors what `formatCsv` already does" only holds for the record path, since `formatCsv` escapes nested values for arrays too (csv.ts:17-19).

samples.summary: `cells batch` parses `--data`/stdin JSON outside the try block, so malformed input becomes an unhandled promise rejection instead of the structured error body the diff's own rationale relies on
samples.evidence: cells.ts:117-127: `cells = JSON.parse(dataStr)` (line 119) and the stdin `JSON.parse` (line 126) sit above the `try` that starts at line 139. In an async commander action a throw here rejects the returned promise; `bin.ts` (line 27, `program.parse()`) installs no rejection handler, so `wafflebase sheets cells batch doc --data '{'` prints a raw stack trace / triggers an unhandled-rejection crash rather than the `{ "error": { ... } }` body §8.1 promises. Pre-existing, but it is the exact failure mode the schema.ts hunk of this change cites ("bin.ts has no top-level handler") and adjacent to the modified try blocks.

finding.summary: `cells batch` parses `--data`/stdin JSON outside the try block, so malformed input becomes an unhandled promise rejection instead of the structured error body the diff's own rationale relies on
finding.evidence: cells.ts:117-127: `cells = JSON.parse(dataStr)` (line 119) and the stdin `JSON.parse` (line 126) sit above the `try` that starts at line 139. In an async commander action a throw here rejects the returned promise; `bin.ts` (line 27, `program.parse()`) installs no rejection handler, so `wafflebase sheets cells batch doc --data '{'` prints a raw stack trace / triggers an unhandled-rejection crash rather than the `{ "error": { ... } }` body §8.1 promises. Pre-existing, but it is the exact failure mode the schema.ts hunk of this change cites ("bin.ts has no top-level handler") and adjacent to the modified try blocks.

verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as claimed: in `cells batch`, `JSON.parse(dataStr)` (cells.ts:119) and the stdin `JSON.parse` (cells.ts:126), plus the `for await (const chunk of process.stdin)` loop (cells.ts:123), all sit above the `try` that begins at cells.ts:139, unlike the sibling `get`/`set`/`delete` actions which wrap all fallible work (cells.ts:23, 62, 95). bin.ts:27 uses `program.parse()` with no `parseAsync` and no `process.on('unhandledRejection')`; a repo-wide grep for `unhandledRejection`/`parseAsync`/`process.on(` in packages/cli matches only scripts/debug-cmd.mjs:15, and root.ts:42-59 adds no error hook. So malformed `--data '{'` or malformed stdin throws inside the async action, rejecting an unobserved promise: the user gets a raw stack trace / fatal unhandled rejection instead of the structured `{ error: { code, message } }` body produced by outputError (formatter.ts:78-88). Reachable on a normal input path, in the Correctness lane (unhandled throw / mis-handled failure), so it is not refutable as not-present, already-guarded, or out-of-scope.

searchedFor: grep for imports of ../output/formatter.js in packages/cli
read api-keys.ts, cells.ts, sheets-import.ts, sheets-export.ts, docs.ts, notes.ts, slides.ts action bodies
read docs/tasks/active/20260806-cli-status-ctx-structured-output-lessons.md (call-site audit claim covers only try/catch presence, not pre-mutation validation)
finding.summary: New `default:` throw in `format()` fires *after* side effects at the ~12 unvalidated `output()` call sites; only status/ctx/schema validate `--format` up front
finding.evidence: formatter.ts:51-55 now throws `InvalidFormatError` from `format()` for any value outside json|table|csv. Only the three commands touched by this diff call `parseOutputFormat(opts.format)` before doing work; every other caller still passes the raw `opts.format` straight into `output()` after the request has already been executed (api-keys.ts:20 `output(res.data, opts.format, false)` after `createApiKey`, cells.ts:66/92/139 after writes, sheets-import.ts:91 after the import, docs/slides/notes create/update). With e.g. `wafflebase api-keys create ci --format jsonl`, the key is created server-side, `format()` throws, `outputError` prints INVALID_FORMAT and sets `process.exitCode = 1` — so a command that succeeded reports failure, and for `api-keys create` the raw key (shown only once, per the comment on line 19) is destroyed with no way to recover it. An agent seeing exit 1 will reasonably retry the mutation, duplicating writes. The guard added in this change (parseOutputFormat before any work) is exactly the right shape but was applied to only 3 of the call sites.

verdict.reason: The finding claims only status/ctx/schema call parseOutputFormat before doing work, and specifically that api-keys.ts:20 passes raw opts.format into output() after createApiKey. Reading the file shows the opposite: api-keys.ts:23 calls parseOutputFormat(opts.format) BEFORE the await on line 24 that mints the key, with a comment explicitly stating the ordering rationale, and line 27 passes the narrowed fmt. Every other cited site is guarded the same way and in the same pre-mutation position: cells.ts:63 before setCell, cells.ts:96 before deleteCell, cells.ts:140 before batchCells, sheets-import.ts:50 before the import, and docs/notes/slides/tabs/api-keys list+revoke. sheets.ts and sheets-export.ts contain no output()/opts.format usage at all, so they are not unguarded paths either. The premise (guard applied to only 3 call sites) is false, so the described crash-after-side-effect path does not exist.
